The plumbing beneath it is forced by scale, which reduces every coefficient modulo the prime as it goes, so a scaled combination is only CONGRUENT to the scaled sum rather than equal to it; rawSum_scale_mod discharges that congruence and sum_mod_congr lifts it across a matrix row

phase: Phase 2 — coefficient count: normal form pinned, program total decomposed
invariant: the coefficient count of a never-materialize encoding has to be taken over NORMALIZED rows: applyMatrix concatenates and never aggregates, so counting raw entries would measure the intermediate representation rather than the encoding. normalize_nodup and normalize_length_of_nodup upgrade normalize from 'at most as long' (normalize_length_le, already had) to 'exactly one entry per referenced column', which is what makes a count exact rather than an upper bound. canonicalProgram_termCount then decomposes the program total into receipts: 4 * sum of scheduled combination sizes + 8 * 86 + sum of final-state lane sizes + 2 * 8. sboxRows_termCount is where the per-S-box shape comes from — the input combination occupies four operand positions (both operands of the squaring row, the multiplier of the cubing and seventh-power rows) and the other eight entries are singletons
result: the program's coefficient total is derived as a receipt fold, reduced to two quantities: the sum of the 86 scheduled combination sizes and the sum of the 8 final-state lane sizes
distinction_recorded: TERM COUNT is not NONZERO-COEFFICIENT COUNT and the two are separated rather than conflated. A normalized entry can still carry a coefficient that vanishes modulo the prime if matrix products cancel, so nonzero <= rowTermCount, with equality exactly when no cancellation occurs. Density of both matrices (externalMatrix_nonzero, internalMatrix_nonzero) rules out the trivial source of zeros but not cancellation in a sum of products. sboxRows_termCount confines the uncertainty: eight of every S-box's entries are singletons carrying coefficient 1 and are certainly nonzero, so only the four copies of the input combination are in question. Proving no cancellation over the concrete constants is a separate arithmetic obligation, named POSEIDON2-NO-CANCELLATION
remaining_dependency: ordered queue. (2) POSEIDON2-NO-CANCELLATION, if an exact nonzero count rather than an upper bound is wanted. (3) benchmark against production, which additionally needs production's own coefficient count — an artifact measurement not yet taken, and not to be inferred from its row count. (4) scoped minimality. Phase 3 is unblocked

phase: Phase 2 — field-canonical normal form; two review claims verified against the goal text
invariant: a second external review found a defect neither I nor the first review had recorded: normalize adds coefficients as UNBOUNDED naturals, so a merged coefficient can exceed the prime and one congruent to zero is retained. Neither affects lcEval, but the first breaks any eventual row-level equality against Rust, which stores canonical residues, and the second means the entry count bounds the nonzero count rather than being it. POSEIDON2-NO-CANCELLATION as I had framed it covered only the second and missed the first entirely. fieldNormalize reduces every coefficient and drops the zeros; lcEval_fieldNormalize proves it semantics-preserving, fieldNormalize_canonical that every stored entry is a canonical residue, fieldNormalize_nonzero that none vanishes. Its length IS the nonzero count
result: two blockers addressed. The field-canonical normal form is proved correct, and nodup_length_eq — the list primitive core does not provide and which blocked the partial-family support count — is proved, together with normalize_length_eq_witness which turns a support characterization directly into an exact length

The review is also right that row VALUES are the wrong ownership ABI: position is what a row program has, and two receipts emitting equal rows is degenerate but not incoherent. Every such evaluation decomposes into K multiplications and K additions, additions are linear and free under the never-materialize discipline, so the entire row cost is a multiple of this gadget. Pinning it fixes the multiplier before any identity is written
non_vacuity_checked: evaluated K.mul on a concrete pair and compared against the emitted formulas rather than trusting the algebra. K.mul (3,5) (2,7) = (251, 31); outLow gives 3*2 + 7*(5*7) = 251 and outHigh gives 3*7 + 5*2 = 31. Without this the soundness theorems could have been proved about a formula that is not the extension's multiplication — the X squared equals 7 coefficient is exactly where that would go wrong
artifact_independence: built only on R1CS/Core/Semantics (Row, RowHolds, Satisfies) and Core/Projection/Polynomial (K, K.ops), both Lean-owned. No Artifacts module in the closure, which is the property cycle 235 showed RecursiveRows fails
named_choice_deferred: schoolbook four products versus Karatsuba three. Karatsuba is a 25 percent row saving on every projection multiplication and the projection check is expected to dominate. Not taken here because the three-product form changes which intermediate values exist, so it must be selected once for the whole projection encoding rather than per gadget — the same discipline that made the Poseidon2 S-box chain a single global choice. Selecting it after identities are written would invalidate their frame layouts, so this is a prerequisite for any NIFS row count rather than a later optimization

phase: Phase 5 — KMUL-PRODUCT-COUNT decided and implemented
invariant: one Goldilocks-quadratic multiplication emits exactly three rows and allocates three auxiliary columns, under Karatsuba. Both output coordinates stay linear in those products and emit nothing
decision_and_why: Karatsuba strictly dominates, so the project's rows-first optimization order never had to be consulted. The naive objection is that its third row takes summed operands and carries 2|cL| and 2|cR| entries instead of |cL| and |cR|. Working the totals: schoolbook is 4|cL| + 4|cR| + 4 across four rows, Karatsuba is 4|cL| + 4|cR| + 3 across three. One entry cheaper, and outHigh spends that one back on its extra term. why_these_two: the witness is built inside out, deepest frame first. That is the link that will discharge KMulHonest.Fresh at every step, and it is why the allocator had to be built before completeness rather than alongside it

phase: Phase 5 - pricing the Lucas derivation before committing to it
invariant: the Lucas derivation from the certificate needs one expensive step - that an injective map between finite sets of equal cardinality is surjective - and the tree has no finite-cardinality machinery to reuse
the_derivation: from ord(7) = q-1 the powers 7^0 to 7^(q-2) are q-1 distinct residues, each a unit. Units sit inside {1..q-1} which has exactly q-1 elements, so every element is a unit. If q = a*b with 1 < a < q then a is a unit, so a*c = 1, so b = b*a*c = (a*b)*c = 0, contradicting 1 < b < q. Hence q is prime and Euclid's lemma follows
the_expensive_step: q-1 distinct elements inside a set of size q-1 therefore exhaust it. The tree has no Finset, no Fintype.card and no pigeonhole lemma - every List.Nodup use is list-level and local. Searched by concept and by name across Nightstream, not by one filename. It also cannot be decided: the set has about 1.8e19 elements, so it must be a genuine proof rather than a kernel computation, which is the opposite of the certificate arithmetic that reduces in 0.19 seconds
verdict: route OPEN, not blocked. Pigeonhole is strictly easier than primality, so this is not a reduction to a statement of comparable strength. But it is a few hundred lines of general-purpose finite-cardinality development with no protocol content, sitting off the Phase 4 critical path

The correction is one of size, not direction: the core is real and it is smaller than its guard surface - 268 lines of which the great majority are shape guards and error formatting.
the_four_carriers: every entry of the public X matrix via split_b_matrix_k (D * m_in values); every lane of every y_ring row via the y_lhs loop (t * d_pad); every lane of y_zcol when enforce_y_zcol_recomposition (d_pad); every aux_openings entry. All four are the same relation.
why_two_rows: b is public, so b^i are public constants and scaling is a coefficient rewrite rather than a multiplication. Nothing is allocated and no product row is emitted for the sum. A K-valued recomposition over k_rho=14 children looks like it needs 14 extension multiplications; it needs none, because the scalars live in the base field and act coordinatewise. The whole cost is the equality against the parent: two rows, one per extension coordinate.
conformance_was_proved_not_assumed: the encoder emits Horner form c0 + b*(c1 + b*(...)); verify_dec_public builds an explicit table with p_k *= b_k and then sums pow_i * child_i. Same function, different expression. powerSumFrom transcribes the verifier's loop accumulator and all, and powerSumFrom_eq_hornerValue proves agreement from an arbitrary starting power, with powerSum_one at the verifier's p_k = 1. Without it the encoding would be checking a relation the verifier does not check.
not_vacuous: hornerValue 2 [1,1,1] = 7 and hornerValue 3 [1,1,1] = 13, so neither side of the conformance theorem is constant in the base.
negative_controls: the honest fixture is accepted, then four independent mutations are each rejected: parent low coordinate, parent high coordinate, one child digit, and the base itself (2 -> 3). The base control confirms the coefficient rewrite is load-bearing rather than decorative.
ten_of_ten: constructive row program (recompositionRows); derived count (recompositionRows_length, = 2); row ownership (KEquality.rows_eq_map_owners); column ownership (recompositionColumns = [], nodup); conservation (recompositionRows_conservation via mentions_recomposeComb); soundness (recompositionRows_sound); honest completeness (recompositionRows_honest, under the caller's own assignment since nothing is allocated); Typed.Cost (recompositionCost); fail-closed axiom guard (23 measured reports); spec and this entry.
syntactic_size_is_not_row_cost: the emitted combination's length is the sum of the children's and grows with k; its row cost does not. Prompt section 4.7 - neither figure is evidence about the other.

invariant: Satisfies (canonicalProgram canonicalLayout constants) z <-> forall column < 361, z column = honestAssignment constants (inputValues canonicalLayout z) column, under z 0 = 1 and canonical residues.
supersedes: POSEIDON2-EXEC-SPEC-SHAPE (cycle 312) recorded that permutationProgram_exec_iff_spec does not exist and its literal form would be false. That was right about the literal form and wrong to stop there. The literal form has output equality on the right; the true and stronger form has agreement with the honest execution on every column, and soundness does establish it.
why_the_literal_form_is_false: an assignment can carry the correct S-box output while carrying a wrong intermediate. Demonstrated on a one-S-box fixture that is otherwise accepted: mutating only the square intermediate is rejected while the output column is provably unchanged; same for the sixth. An outputs=reference biconditional would have accepted both, which is to say it would claim the encoding accepts assignments it must reject.
what_made_uniqueness_available: canonicalProgram_sbox_chains forces all four chain columns per S-box - square, fourth, sixth, output - not merely the output. Every allocated column is one of those four or an output port, so pinning them pins the whole witness. Had the chain lemma forced only the S-box output, uniqueness would be false and two separate directions would have been the ceiling.
the_one_missing_piece: scheduleOf_eval: lcEval z (scheduleOf i) = sboxInputValue constants (inputValues z) i for an arbitrary satisfying z. Poseidon2Honest.honest_scheduleOf proves it for the honest assignment only, through honest_initialState and siblings; scheduleOf_eval is its mirror through the round inductions initialState_eval, partialState_eval, terminalState_eval. Neither existing direction had it.
also_new: rowHolds_congr and satisfies_congr (satisfaction depends on an assignment only through mentioned columns); canonicalProgram_conservation (whole-program conservation for the raw program, previously stated only for the normalized one); sboxColumn_forced (every chain column equals its honest value).
scope: the width-8 permutation program only. Says nothing about the sponge, domain separation, binding, or random-oracle security. Prompt 4.6 - arithmetic correctness proves neither of the two hashes' security contracts.
input_ports_are_shared_reads: inputValues is the assignment restricted to the input ports, so their arm of the biconditional is definitional. phase: Phase 2 naming + Phase 3 - hashPrior and hashNext as emitted row programs
invariant: hashPrior and hashNext are the fixed-23 sponge placed at disjoint column windows: 2464 rows and 2549 allocated columns each, bases 0 and 2550, with the constant wire a shared read belonging to neither owner.
phase2_naming: permutationProgram_exec_iff_spec now exists as a theorem at that exact name, in Poseidon2Uniqueness. canonicalProgram IS permutationProgram at the canonical schedule and final state, so the restatement is definitional in the program spelling and not in the claim; what makes it true is the uniqueness proved in cycle 328.
what_was_missing_in_phase3: Poseidon2Sponge23 already owned absorption, padding, rate, capacity and the digest. What it did not own is placement: it is written at fixed absolute columns - seven permutation blocks of stride 361, then 23 preimage columns at 2527. Sufficient for one hash; the step program contains two, and two instances of a fixed-column program collide on every column they use. The obligation not already discharged was therefore exactly: place two instances so that distinct owners never collide is a theorem, and carry soundness and completeness across the placement.
derived_numbers: sponge column window 2550 = inputBase + sponge23Fields, evaluated; 2549 columns owned per instance = window minus the shared constant wire; 2464 rows per instance from program_length through List.length_map; hashPriorBase 0 and hashNextBase 2550. Every one derived from the emitted program or the sponge's own definitions, none measured from an artifact.
transport: rowHolds_pull_iff carries both directions. hashProgram_pull reduces satisfaction of a placed instance to satisfaction of the sponge under pullAssignment z (relocate base), so program_computes_digest applies unchanged. pull_honestAssignment shows the placed honest witness pulls back to the sponge's own, so honest_satisfies transports. Conservation is stated as what the placement does - every column of a relocated row is the relocation of an Allocated source column - and composes with program_conservation; the placement introduces nothing.
no_domain_tag: Vocabulary's own docstring states that hashPrior and hashNext have the same semantics and differ only in ownership; both invoke machine.hash on the same record shape with the same callInputs. This encoding does not invent a separator - adding one would change a mapped definition, a change-control decision and not a formalization one. What separation exists is the sponge's padding rule, which absorbs a single 1 and is what makes preimages of different lengths distinct. Recorded as POSEIDON2-HASH-NO-DOMAIN-TAG so a reader can tell it was checked rather than overlooked.

phase: Phase 4 - the batched low-norm check, Pi_DEC's dominant row cost
invariant: The low-norm check over many digits is one row program with one witness; 2 rows and 1 column per digit; and both WellFormed arms are necessary rather than decorative.
why_this_is_the_dominant_cost: Pi_DEC decomposes every entry of the public X matrix into k_rho = 14 balanced base-2 digits, so the per-digit low-norm check runs D * m_in * 14 times. Everything else in the decomposition is allocation-free.
rows_batch_trivially_the_witness_does_no: KLowNorm.lowNormWitness writes one square to one allocated column and each digit needs its own. Composing the writes is sound only under WellFormed: distinct (the allocated columns are Nodup, else the outer write clobbers the inner square and the inner digit's rows fail) and fresh (no checked combination reads any allocated column, not merely its own, else its value is changed by another digit's write).
both_arms_demonstrated: Three fixtures, all with honest cubes under the same base assignment so that no failure is the cube test failing. Distinct columns with no cross-reads: nodup yes, satisfied yes. Two digits sharing column 3 with squares 1 and 0: nodup no, satisfied no. Tail digit reading the head's square column: nodup YES, satisfied no. The third isolates fresh rather than distinct, because its allocation is collision-free. Between them the controls show that exact column ownership with no collision is load-bearing here and not a naming convention.

phase: Phase 4 - Pi_DEC assembled
invariant: Pi_DEC's decomposition algebra is one emitted row program with one honest witness; its row count is a fold over five per-atom receipts; and only its digit range check allocates.
the_four_carriers_are_one_call: xEntries, yRingLanes, yZcolLanes and auxOpenings are concatenated into a single recompositionsRows call rather than four, because PIDEC-RECOMPOSITION proved they are one relation. Emitting four calls would have made the same rows look like four separate obligations.
count_is_folded_and_checked: 2*|recompositions| + 2*|xDigits| + |inactiveX| + 2*|yRingPadding| + 2*|consistency|, every term a per-atom receipt. On a fixture with 4 recompositions, 2 digits, 3 inactive entries, 1 padded lane and 1 consistency pair the emitted program has 19 rows and cost.recurringRows is 19 - derived from the emitted list first, then cross-checked against the cost tuple rather than asserted from it.
one_allocator_is_the_whole_composition_p: Every atom but one is allocation-free: recompositions, zero checks, padding and consistency read carried values and write nothing. KLowNormBatch is the sole allocator, one column per digit. So the assembled honest witness IS the batch's witness - there is nothing else to extend - and every other part must still hold under that extension. It does, but only if no other part reads an allocated column, which is the Fresh hypothesis. PIDEC-LOWNORM-BATCH already demonstrated that a violated freshness arm makes a batch unsatisfiable even when its allocation is collision-free, so Fresh is not bookkeeping.
completeness_is_soundness_converse: Each field of the Honest structure is verbatim the conclusion of the corresponding rows_sound_* theorem, so the recipe is complete for precisely the transitions it accepts - no gap in either direction.

phase: Phase 3 commitments + Phase 4 selection boundary
invariant: runningCheck and freshCheck are setup selections; two lawful RelationChecks over the same carriers give opposite verdicts on the same argument, so no row program for them can be derived from this encoding.
the_selection_surface_is_now_complete: step, nifsVerify, runningCheck, freshCheck. All four are setup-selected and none is derivable. allRecipes and N_canonical are downstream of all four. This is a section 7 blocked route: every alternative identified for these four is also blocked, because the blockage is a protocol input rather than a missing proof.
why_this_is_not_the_vacuous_shape: NifsCompletionBoundary withdrew a theorem of the form 'X does not determine Y' for independent X and Y, which is provable for every X and says nothing. These statements fix everything except the checks and compare two concrete inhabitants at one concrete argument, so what varies is exactly the object the claim is about. lawful_checkers_still_disagree adds that both inhabitants satisfy their own _iff fields, so the disagreement is not an artefact of an unconstrained field.
receipt_carried_verdict: The one native-conformance instantiation, Implementation/Rust/CanonicalConformance/OneSlot.lean, defines runningReceiptCheck as receipt.accepted conjoined with a field match, and terminalRelations defines runningHolds as that Bool being true. In that lane the relation IS 'the receipt says accepted'. The project rule is that digests compress but never authorise. Scope stated precisely: this is a fact about the Lean conformance model of the native F-prime lane, NOT a claim that shipping Rust fails to enforce a frozen relation - determining which requires reading the Rust terminal path, which has not been done. Recorded as TERMINAL-CHECK-RECEIPT-CARRIED so a future runningCheck recipe is not built on the assumption that this instantiation is the authority.
phase3_commitments: Poseidon2HashRecipe now states and discharges its own commitments rather than only consuming them: rate 4, capacity 4, rate+capacity=width, digest within rate, arity 23, chunking 5*4+3, seven permutation calls, absorption never writes capacity. Each is discharged from the sponge; none re-proved. The point is auditability - a reader checking hashPrior should see what it promises without reconstructing which sponge it was built on.
separation_sharpened: Two new theorems replace prose. committed_single_arity: the recipe admits exactly one preimage length, so the padding rule's length-distinguishing job is vacuous here - there are no two lengths to distinguish. This is STRONGER than the earlier claim that padding is what separates; at fixed arity it separates nothing because nothing needs separating. digest_independent_of_placement: two placed instances compute the same digest from the same preimage, which is the formal content of 'hashPrior and hashNext have the same semantics'. Together with POSEIDON2-HASH-NO-DOMAIN-TAG the answer is exact: what separates a prior digest from a next digest is entirely the preimage content, and two call sites hashing equal 23-field preimages obtain equal digests.

phase: Phase 4 - the fold-digest checks, and a corrected dependency
invariant: Neither fold-digest check needs a hash. Consistency is a base-field lane equality, one row per lane. Canonicality has no row program at all, because every value this row layer can carry is already a canonical residue.
supersedes: Cycles 326 through 332 all carried 'fold digest canonicity and consistency, needing Poseidon2' in remaining_dependency. That was wrong, and wrong in a way worth naming: the dependency was inherited from the word 'digest' rather than read off the validators. validate_fold_digest_consistency is equality between child and parent fold_digest; validate_fold_digest_canonical reads each eight-byte lane little-endian as a u64 and rejects it when value >= F::ORDER_U64. A range check. No hash in either.
canonicality_has_no_row_and_that_is_a_th: lcEval reduces modulo the prime, so carried_is_canonical gives lcEval z comb < goldilocksP for every z and comb. no_canonicality_violation states the consequence as the non-existence of a violating assignment rather than as a comment, because 'this needs no rows' is a claim about every assignment and should be checkable as one. Emitting rows would fabricate a constraint the encoding cannot violate - the same defect as emitting rows for a list-length assertion, and the trap prompt section 3 names. What the check does in Rust is guard the decoder against a byte string that does not decode to field elements.
one_row_per_lane: A fold-digest lane is a base-field value, not an extension element, so a lane equality costs one row where a K equality costs two. Derived from the emitted list via List.length_map, not asserted.

invariant: RETRACTED. The receipt-carried verdict observed in cycle 332 is a differential-test schema's recorded side, not the protocol authorising on a carried bit. There is no production defect.
what_was_wrong: Cycle 332 recorded that Implementation/Rust/CanonicalConformance/OneSlot.lean defines runningHolds as receipt.accepted conjoined with a field match, and flagged it against the project rule that digests compress but never authorise. phase: Phase 4 - the transcript row program
invariant: The Fiat-Shamir duplex as an emitted row program: one permutation per round, rounds*352 rows and rounds*344 auxiliaries, overwrite absorption emitting no row, and the chain carrying round r's output ports into round r+1's entry.
the_entry_is_where_the_mode_lives: Each entry lane is the absorbed column alone when written (entry_overwritten), the previous round's output port alone when not (entry_carried), or the empty combination at round zero which is the all-zero initial state (entry_initial). Neither is a row. Same 'absorption is free' fact the sponge has, but the combination differs: add mode carries [(chunk,1),(previousPort,1)] where this carries one term or the other. TRANSCRIPT-MODE-BOUNDARY proves those denote different values from any carried state; here the difference is visible in the emitted syntax, which is where an encoder can actually get it wrong.
the_cursor_is_static: Poseidon2Duplex's cursor is a runtime value; in a row program it is not. The absorb schedule is fixed at encoding time, so no row implements the 'if absorbed >= RATE then permute' guard - the encoder has already placed the permutations where the guard would have fired. Schedule is that parameter, and a caller supplying one inconsistent with the duplex's cursor arithmetic gets a program that is internally sound and models something else. Named as the caller's obligation rather than assumed away.
eight_of_ten: Constructive row program, derived count, row ownership, column ownership, soundness, chain, Typed.Cost, fail-closed guard, spec and ledger - yes. Honest completeness and conservation are NOT proved; they follow Poseidon2Sponge's pattern and need its per-call witness machinery lifted to the overwrite entry, which is not done. Stated in the module header and named as TRANSCRIPT-RECIPE-OPEN rather than left for a reader to infer from absence. Claiming ten would be the subtotal-presented-as-a-total defect.

invariant: The remaining step for transcript row ownership is not bookkeeping. entryAt reads the previous round's output ports, so a row of round r legitimately mentions columns of window r-1 as well as window r, and single-window containment is false for this recipe.
corrects: Cycle 358 called the remaining step 'bookkeeping rather than a new argument'. That was wrong. The natural argument - all of a row's columns lie in one window, so two windows force the rounds equal - does not apply, because the chaining that makes the duplex a duplex is exactly what defeats single-window containment. chain_value is the theorem that a round reads the previous round's output; it is the point of the construction, not a defect.
what_the_argument_actually_needs: Two facts. First, every row touches its own window: the four S-box rows target sboxColumn (layouts r) index slot and the binding row targets (layouts r).outputPort lane, both in window r, with mentions_normalizeRow carrying this through normalization. Second, every row's columns lie in window r-1 union window r, which needs the entry classification per round, and transcriptRows_conservation supplies it only with the round existentially bound. With both, a shared row puts a window-r column inside window r'-1 union window r', and disjointness forces r in {r'-1, r'} and symmetrically r' in {r-1, r}, closing only after ruling out the crossed case.

phase: Phase 3 - the separator survives absorption
invariant: A difference between two preimages survives absorption into the state, not only the chunk decomposition.
what_the_docstring_claimed: chunkAt_determines proves two preimages with the same chunks are the same preimage. Its docstring concluded 'whatever the profile distinguishes upstream survives absorption'. Chunking and absorption are two steps: chunking arranges a preimage into blocks, absorption folds a block into the state. A recipe with injective chunking could still absorb two distinct chunks into one state, and the separator would be lost before a single permutation ran - a structural failure, not a cryptographic one. Nothing ruled it out.
the_missing_step: absorbChunk adds the chunk into the rate lane modulo the prime, and addition is injective: two canonical values absorbed at the same lane of the same state give different lanes exactly when they differ. Stated at a lane rather than on whole chunks because that is where a separator lands - one slot, not a block.
theorems: Poseidon2Sponge.absorbChunk_injective_at_lane - absorption is injective in the chunk, lane by lane
Poseidon2HashRecipe.separator_survives_absorption - the state after absorbing chunk zero differs between a preimage and its slot-zero increment
where_the_separation_chain_now_stands: preimages differ at slot zero (separatedPreimage_differs); chunk zero differs (separatedPreimage_reaches_chunk_zero); state after absorbing chunk zero differs (separator_survives_absorption); digest differs - Poseidon2's, not this recipe's. The chain is arithmetic-complete: every step that can be settled by arithmetic is. That sharpens what 'domain separation is split across layers' means - the split sits precisely at the permutation, not vaguely at 'the profile'.
how_it_was_found: By reading a docstring against the theorem under it. The theorem is about chunking; the sentence claimed absorption. Second cycle running in which prose asserted a conclusion no theorem carried - cycle 386's was a commitments header naming padding, this one a docstring naming absorption. a_downstream_break_that_was_not_mine: After adding to Poseidon2Sponge the aggregate gate failed in PiRlcCanonicalSymbolicMachine with two omega errors. Removing my addition and rebuilding gave NINE errors in the same file - a different failure, which is the signal that the module was not in a state my change controlled. mtime confirmed it: the file had been written 12 seconds earlier by the concurrent Track A session, mid-edit. The gate went green at 3222 once they finished. Recorded as method: when a downstream module breaks after your change, remove the change and rebuild; a DIFFERENT failure means the module is not yours to fix, and the wrong move is to start repairing someone else's intermediate state.
